symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independently sampled units in the stated finite-sample frontier.

symbols.name: \Delta_0
symbols.def: A fixed upper bound on the released radial bin width.

symbols.name: \Delta
symbols.def: The known width of every floor-rounded radial bin.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: The known common constant in the two side-specific point-anchored boundary envelopes.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The prescribed error probability for honest confidence intervals.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: The target point, normalized to \(b=(0,0)\).

symbols.name: e_1
symbols.def: The unit vector \(e_1=(1,0)\) used only to specify the uniform half-disc least-favorable subclass.

symbols.name: \mathcal D
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1\}\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The raw location score, which is sampled but not released to the analyst.

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R=\lVert X-b\rVert_2\).

symbols.name: Y(0)
symbols.def: The bounded potential outcome under control.

symbols.name: Y(1)
symbols.def: The bounded potential outcome under treatment.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A one-unit law for the latent score and potential outcomes; treatment and the observed outcome are induced by sharp assignment and consistency.

symbols.name: Q_\Delta
symbols.def: \(Q_\Delta(r)=\Delta\lfloor r/\Delta\rfloor\).

symbols.name: \rho_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(\rho_{n,\Delta}=\max\{h_n,\Delta\}\).

symbols.name: K_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(K_{n,\Delta}=\lceil h_n/\Delta\rceil\).

symbols.name: H_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(H_{n,\Delta}=K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\).

symbols.name: I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{n,\gamma}(s)
symbols.def: For any positive integer trial count \(k\), \(I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\gamma}(s)\) is the equal-tailed exact \(1-\gamma\) binomial confidence interval after \(s\) successes in \(k\) trials.

symbols.name: c_0
symbols.def: A fixed class constant lower-bounding each side probability in a radius-\(H\) neighborhood by \(c_0H^2\).

symbols.name: \mathcal X_{t,P}
symbols.def: The known Borel partition satisfies \(\mathcal X_{0,P}\cap\mathcal X_{1,P}=\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal X_{0,P}\cup\mathcal X_{1,P}=\mathcal D\); the local-mass condition implies that \(b\) lies in the closure of both sides.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The bounded realized outcome under the sharp assignment.

symbols.name: Z_\Delta
symbols.def: \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\); neither \(X\), the polar angle, nor raw \(R\) is observed.

symbols.name: S_{t,n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}Y_i\).

symbols.name: \mathcal T_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: All law-independent estimators measurable with respect to the released sample only.

symbols.name: N_{t,n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The observed-count ratio with fixed zero-count fallback constructed in \(\mathrm{def:bin\text{-}aware\text{-}estimator}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

symbols.name: C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
symbols.def: The conditional-Hoeffding bounded-outcome interval with sidewise spatial Lipschitz enlargement constructed in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\).

symbols.name: \theta_t
symbols.def: The number in \([0,1]\) anchoring side \(t\) at the fixed boundary point \(b\).

symbols.name: \mu_t
symbols.def: \(\mu_t(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=x]\) for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point, with the declared boundary value \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).
symbols.role: outcome regression and boundary anchor carrier

symbols.name: \mathcal P_L
symbols.type: unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary law class
symbols.def: The one-unit full-data laws with the stated known side partition, two-sided quadratic local mass, outcomes supported on \([0,1]\) with conditional means \(\mu_t\), consistency, and side-specific point-anchored envelopes.

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The explicit embedded uniform-half-disc pair constructed in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).
symbols.role: joint minimax and honest-length lower certificate

symbols.name: m_t
symbols.type: radial profile for constructed least-favorable laws
symbols.sig: \([0,1]\to[1/4,3/4]\) on the embedded uniform half-disc subclass
symbols.def: For a constructed radial law, \(m_t(r)\) denotes the profile satisfying \(\mu_t(x)=m_t(\lVert x-b\rVert_2)\); it is not a restriction on every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\).

symbols.name: \tau_P(b)
symbols.def: \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0=\mu_1(b)-\mu_0(b)\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The squared risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
symbols.def: The interval class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
symbols.def: The width criterion constructed in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}width}\).

symbols.name: P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}
symbols.def: The two bivariate laws constructed in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).
symbols.role: exact nonidentification witness in a least-favorable subclass

symbols.name: \mathcal Q_\Delta
symbols.space: sets of probability laws on the released observation space
symbols.def: The image \(\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\).

symbols.name: I_\Delta
symbols.def: The set of structural point boundary effects compatible with a fixed one-unit released law, defined in \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\).

symbols.name: \omega_\Delta
symbols.def: The supremum over attainable released laws of the diameter of \(I_\Delta\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:released\text{-}identified\text{-}set}\).

assumptions.condition: \((X_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
For the fixed class constant \(c_0\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\) for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).
There is a known Borel side partition \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) of \(\mathcal D\) such that \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely under \(P\).

standard.name: sharp assignment across a known bivariate boundary

assumptions.condition:
For every \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) satisfying \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2.
\]

definitions.name: Unknown-design bivariate bounded-outcome point-anchored boundary class
definitions.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\) is supported on \([0,1]\) and has mean \(\mu_t(x)\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

definitions.name: Rounded-radius observation experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n}),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

definitions.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
definitions.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

definitions.name: Rounded-radius minimax risks
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b)|\) and \(\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b))^2]\).

definitions.name: Honest closed bounded confidence-interval class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)=\{C:C\text{ is a closed bounded interval-valued, }\sigma(Z_\Delta^n)\text{-measurable map and }\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb P_P(\tau_P(b)\in C)\geq1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-Hoeffding interval
definitions.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\).  When \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), put
\[
 \overline Y_t=\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k,
 \qquad
 r_{k,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2k}},
 \qquad
 [\ell_t,u_t]=\bigl[\max\{0,\overline Y_t-r_{k,\alpha}\},\min\{1,\overline Y_t+r_{k,\alpha}\}\bigr].
\]
With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

definitions.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
definitions.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

definitions.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

definitions.name: Released-law identified set and maximal fiber diameter
definitions.construction:
For \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), let
\[
 \mathcal Q_\Delta=\{\mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta):P\in\mathcal P_L\}.
\]
For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), define the nonempty release-fiber identified set and its diameter by
\[
 I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L\ \text{and}\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q)=\sup_{a,a'\in I_\Delta(Q)}|a-a'|.
\]
The maximal population ambiguity of the rounded release is
\[
 \omega_\Delta=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam} I_\Delta(Q).
\]

definitions.name: Sharp release-fiber endpoint-program handle
definitions.construction: Reduce each release fiber to two side-specific extremal programs over latent first-bin conditional-mean functions whose released bin averages are fixed by \(Q\), whose values lie in \([0,1]\), and whose deviations from their boundary anchors satisfy the point-anchored \(L\)-Lipschitz envelope; then couple the two endpoint programs through \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\).

statements.statement:
For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every release law \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\) has positive probability on each first-bin side event \(\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0\}\), and
\[
 2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta.
\]
Consequently, the full-data causal functional \(\tau_P(b)\) is generally not point identified from a fixed-\(\Delta\) released law, and its worst release-fiber diameter is of order \(\Delta\).
statements.justification: This is the headline partial-identification result: it quantifies the population ambiguity created by the rounded release before finite-sample error is considered.
statements.gap: DaveziesLeBarbanchon2017 restores scalar-RD identification using auxiliary discrepancy data, and GerardRokkanenRothe2020 sharply bounds effects under latent manipulation types; neither evaluates the release fiber generated by a known annular map with no auxiliary true-score sample over the stated bivariate point-anchored class.
statements.consumer: It tells analysts and data stewards how much fixed-precision radial release alone can vary the latent point boundary effect before sampling error is considered.

statements.statement: Characterize the exact endpoint map \(Q\mapsto(\inf I_\Delta(Q),\sup I_\Delta(Q))\) for every attainable released law \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\), and determine the exact value of the maximal diameter \(\omega_\Delta\) over \(\mathcal P_L\).
statements.justification: Exact fiber endpoints would turn the order-sharp ambiguity bound into a release-law-specific sharp partial-identification procedure.
statements.gap: The available results bound the worst fiber between explicit multiples of \(\Delta\). GerardRokkanenRothe2020 gives sharp endpoints for manipulation-type ambiguity, but neither that paper nor the measurement-error literature supplies the sharp endpoint program for ambiguity induced by this deterministic annular release.
statements.consumer: A data steward could report the narrowest compatible interval for the boundary effect from the released population law rather than only a worst-case order bound.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
statements.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
statements.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
statements.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(L\), \(c_0\), and \(\Delta_0\), such that for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}\leq\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}\) and \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\leq\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\). The upper bounds are attained, up to \(C\), by \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\).
statements.justification: This is the sampling--quantization minimax frontier over the unknown-design bivariate Lipschitz boundary class.
statements.gap: Exact-radius boundary methods and ordinary scalar rounding methods do not derive the latent-annular rate \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) over this superclass.
statements.consumer: The result tells users of the \(\texttt{rd2d}\) R, Python, and Stata workflows when the Ser Pilo Paga analysis is sample-limited or release-precision-limited.

statements.statement: For every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), the interval \(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) is defined for every released sample, satisfies \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb P_P(\tau_P(b)\in C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})\geq1-\alpha\), and obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})]\leq C_{L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\).
statements.justification: Conditional Hoeffding concentration plus sidewise Euclidean Lipschitz enlargement yields a total honest interval for bounded outcomes under unknown design.
statements.gap: Existing ordinary-running-variable intervals do not handle latent annuli, quadratic local mass, empty random side counts, and general bounded outcomes in this release field.
statements.consumer: The interval is directly implementable when an analyst truly receives only outcome, treatment side, and quantized radial distance.

statements.statement: There is a constant \(c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}>0\) such that, for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C)]\geq c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\); hence \(\mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\asymp\rho_{n,\Delta}\).
statements.justification: The expected-length lower bound certifies that even bounded-outcome honest intervals pay exactly the information loss forced by the release protocol.
statements.gap: General modulus and discrete-running-variable results do not evaluate this rounded radial modulus or its \(n^{-1/4}\)-to-\(\Delta\) transition.
statements.consumer: The lower bound certifies the conditional-Hoeffding interval's rate and prevents comparisons that assume unavailable within-bin coordinates.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
statements.justification: One uniform-half-disc Bernoulli pair combines a localized sampling bump and the exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
statements.gap: No cited comparator supplies this single pair for the latent-annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) target displacement.
statements.consumer: The pair is the common same-class lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length.

statements.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\), the conditional outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid B]=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\) and \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Conditional on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\geq1\), list the selected outcomes in increasing sample-index order as \(Y_{t,1}^{\star},\ldots,Y_{t,k}^{\star}\).  They are independent and identically distributed, supported on \([0,1]\), and have common mean \(\nu_t\); moreover,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{j=1}^kY_{t,j}^{\star},\qquad
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right]=\nu_t,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\frac{S_{t,n,\Delta}}k\,\middle|\,N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\right)\leq\frac1{4k}.
\]
Outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass, the conditional sum need not be binomial.
statements.justification: The lemma supplies the conditional iid selected-outcome law, random-count distribution, bounded variance, and point-anchor bias for the bounded-outcome superclass.
statements.gap: The selected sum is not binomial outside the embedded Bernoulli subclass; the usable general statement is conditional iid bounded sampling with a common mean.
statements.consumer: The local estimator uses its variance bound, and the total interval uses its conditional product law.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), there is at most one \(a\in[0,1]\) such that \(|\mu_t(x)-a|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\). Consequently, the declared \(\theta_t\) and \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\) are well-defined functionals of \(P\).
statements.justification: The point anchor must be a functional of the law, not an arbitrary version choice, for the boundary contrast to be a well-defined causal estimand.
statements.gap: The uniqueness step is specific to combining an almost-everywhere point envelope with positive side mass at every shrinking radius.
statements.consumer: The identified set, risk, and coverage statements use the uniquely determined boundary anchor contrast.

statements.statement:
Let \(k\geq1\), and let \(W_1,\ldots,W_k\) be independent random variables satisfying \(0\leq W_j\leq1\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[W_j]=p\) for every \(j\).  Then, for every \(r\) satisfying \(0<r<1-p\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(\frac1k\sum_{j=1}^kW_j-p\geq r\right)\leq\exp(-2kr^2).
\]

source.verbatim_statement: If X₁,…,Xₙ are independent and 0≤Xᵢ≤1, then for 0<t<1−μ, Pr{X̄−μ≥t}≤e^(−2nt²).

attestation.note: Verified directly from the public JSTOR scan of Hoeffding (1963), Journal of the American Statistical Association 58(301), hosted by Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute at https://www.cs.rpi.edu/academics/courses/spring06/random/hoefding.pdf; inspected original p. 15, Theorem 1 and equation (2.3). DOI and bibliographic identity cross-checked against the Taylor & Francis source-of-record page for 10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830.

statements.justification: This classical one-sided inequality supplies finite-sample concentration for a selected average of independent bounded outcomes.
statements.gap: Hoeffding1963 supplies only the fixed-count concentration leaf; conditioning on a random spatial count and adding point-anchor bias are specific to this note.
statements.consumer: The total conditional-Hoeffding interval invokes the bound on each side and on complemented outcomes.

statements.statement: Along every sequence with \(0<\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\), the unknown-design frontier has minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Along every sequence with \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the corresponding orders are \(\Delta\) and \(\Delta^2\), respectively.
statements.justification: This proposition separates the fine-quantization sampling regime from the coarsening-dominated population-ambiguity regime.
statements.gap: The exact-coordinate literature is a rate benchmark only and does not imply the latent-annular fixed-width result.
statements.consumer: Applied users can diagnose whether sample size or released radial precision is the active limitation.

sampling_model.design: For each law \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), the latent score \(X\) is supported on the unit disc centered at \(b\), with each known assignment side having probability at least \(c_0H^2\) inside every radius \(H\in(0,1/2]\). The design distribution is otherwise unknown; the uniform two-sided half-disc is used only as an embedded lower-bound subclass.
sampling_model.units: The primitive observations \((X_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed, but the analyst receives only \(Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,Q_\Delta(R_i))\). Raw locations, polar angles, and raw radii are excluded from the observation \(\sigma\)-field.
sampling_model.treatment: Assignment is sharp and deterministic through the known Borel side partition: \(T_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and consistency gives \(Y_i=T_iY_i(1)+(1-T_i)Y_i(0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No unit-level treatment-overlap condition is imposed because assignment is deterministic. Instead, the two-sided quadratic local-mass condition requires \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\) for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No design density is estimated. The estimator and interval use only released local counts and outcome sums, the known bin-aligned bandwidth \(H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\rceil\), and the known point-anchor envelope constant \(L\); they do not use a known local side probability.
sampling_model.outcomes: For each side, the potential outcome is supported on \([0,1]\) and has conditional mean \(\mu_t(x)\), whose deviation from its boundary anchor is at most \(L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\). Conditional Bernoulli laws are used only in the embedded alias and joint-pair constructions.

estimand_functional: For \(Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\eta_t(Q)=\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0]\), \(\underline{\theta}_t(Q)=\max\{0,\eta_t(Q)-L\Delta\}\), and \(\overline{\theta}_t(Q)=\min\{1,\eta_t(Q)+L\Delta\}\). Then \(I_\Delta(Q)=\{\tau_P(b):P\in\mathcal P_L,\ \mathcal L_P(Z_\Delta)=Q\}\) satisfies the directly computable certified outer inclusion \(I_\Delta(Q)\subseteq[\underline{\theta}_1(Q)-\overline{\theta}_0(Q),\ \overline{\theta}_1(Q)-\underline{\theta}_0(Q)]\); this is not asserted to be an identified-set equality or a sharp endpoint formula. Moreover, \(2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta:=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_\Delta}\operatorname{diam}I_\Delta(Q)\leq4L\Delta\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Provides estimation, inference, and minimax theory for boundary discontinuity designs using exact point distance; it does not analyze a fixed-\(\Delta\) release fiber.
Studies rounding of an ordinary scalar running variable under moment structure, not loss of raw bivariate coordinates within radial annuli or the radial-Jacobian null direction.

Develops inference for an ordinary discrete running variable, not total conditional-Hoeffding inference for bounded outcomes with unknown bivariate design, quadratic local mass, and latent within-annulus bias.
Supplies general modulus logic but does not evaluate the rounded radial modulus or construct the single sampling-plus-aliasing pair used for this bounded-outcome point-anchored class.
Supplies the bias-enlargement principle, while the present random-count conditional-Hoeffding interval and all-regime expected-length bound are specific to this coarsened release experiment.
Studies causal targets compatible with correctly classified coarsened running scores; it does not recover the fixed latent boundary anchor contrast from outcome, side, and rounded radius alone.

Shows that continuous error in a scalar running variable destroys ordinary RD identification and recovers the LATE using auxiliary discrepancy data under nondifferential-error and completeness/support conditions.
Derives explicitly characterized sharp bounds for causal effects in scalar RD designs whose running variable is manipulated.

tldr: An analyst observes only \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\): bounded outcome, sharp-treatment side, and floor-rounded distance from one fixed boundary point; raw location, polar angle, and raw radius are unavailable. The structural boundary effect is generally only partially identified at fixed release precision. Its release-fiber identified set is \(I_\Delta(Q)\), and the maximal fiber diameter satisfies \(2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta\). The exact first-bin alias \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) supplies the lower bound, while point-anchored Lipschitz envelopes supply the upper bound. Supporting statistical frontiers show that finite-sample absolute risk and honest expected length have order \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\), squared risk has the corresponding squared order, and a total observed-count procedure attains the upper rates.

project_justification.gap: Exact-coordinate boundary methods do not describe the identified set after angle and within-bin radius are removed. Scalar measurement-error methods require auxiliary discrepancy information to restore identification, and manipulation-based partial-identification methods address latent assignment types rather than a known deterministic release map; neither evaluates the release fiber of a fixed bivariate point-boundary effect.
project_justification.niche: The released population law fixes annular outcome averages but not the latent boundary anchors. The radial Jacobian admits an exact first-bin null direction, creating order-\(\Delta\) causal ambiguity even with an infinite sample.
project_justification.fill: The paper fixes the analyst's observation \(\sigma\)-field, defines the release-fiber identified set \(I_\Delta(Q)\), and bounds its worst diameter between \(2c_L\Delta\) and \(4L\Delta\). Matching minimax-risk and honest-length frontiers then separate this population ambiguity from the additional \(n^{-1/4}\) sampling cost.

related_work: DaveziesLeBarbanchon2017 shows in Section 2.3 that continuous measurement error destroys ordinary scalar-RD identification and in Theorem 1 recovers the LATE using an auxiliary treated-sample discrepancy law under nondifferential-error and completeness/support conditions. The present experiment has no auxiliary true-score or discrepancy sample: it applies a known deterministic floor map to radius at a fixed bivariate boundary point and quantifies the compatible-value release fiber with diameter of order \(\Delta\). GerardRokkanenRothe2020 derives explicitly characterized sharp partial-identification bounds for sharp and fuzzy scalar RD under manipulation; its ambiguity comes from latent potentially-assigned and always-assigned types and their identifying restrictions, whereas the ambiguity here comes from suppressing angle and within-bin radius through a known annular release. The target here is a fixed bivariate point-boundary contrast, and only the order-\(\Delta\) maximal fiber diameter is established; exact release-law-specific endpoints remain open. DongKolesar2023Measurement clarifies that correctly classified coarsened scores can identify effects conditional on an observed score; it is an informed comparator because the fixed latent boundary anchor here is generally not identified from side and rounded radius alone. Dong2015Rounding, especially Theorem 1 and equations (4)--(5), integrates latent scalar scores over rounding cells and inverts a polynomial moment map under known within-cell moments; the radial Jacobian here instead exposes a nonparametric first-bin null direction. KolesarRothe2018Discrete shows that clustering by an ordinary discrete running score does not control specification bias and develops smoothness-based coverage methods, but it does not calculate a bivariate annular release fiber. CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance studies exact point distance and is used only as an exact-coordinate comparator. Its theorem statements, proofs, minimax result, and estimator do not transfer to the present experiment, which observes only bounded outcome, treatment side, and floor-rounded radius. The \(n^{-1/4}\) sampling scale and every rounded-release conclusion are derived independently under the present unknown-design, bounded-outcome, point-anchored class; exact distance has no fixed-\(\Delta\) release fiber. ArmstrongKolesar2018Optimal supplies general convex-class modulus logic, and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest supplies the principle of explicit smoothness-bias enlargement; both inform the supporting statistical frontiers rather than the population identified-set claim. KeeleTitiunik2015Geographic explains why retained spatial coordinates matter for boundary effects, and CattaneoTitiunikYu2025Rd2d documents the R, Python, and Stata workflows that can consume the bounds after verifying that raw coordinates, angle, and within-bin radius are unavailable.
interpretation: The causal estimand remains the full-data boundary contrast \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\). At fixed \(\Delta>0\), the released population law need not determine it uniquely: \(I_\Delta(Q)\) records compatible values and \(\omega_\Delta\asymp\Delta\) measures worst release ambiguity. Finite sampling adds the \(n^{-1/4}\) boundary-regression scale. Thus \(\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\) is sample-limited, while \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\) is release-precision-limited.
technical_internal_limitation: The upper fiber bound and statistical upper bounds cover the full unknown-design, \([0,1]\)-bounded-outcome class, but they require the declared quadratic local-mass constant, known side partition, fixed boundary point, and point-anchored Lipschitz envelope. The matching lower bounds embed a uniform half-disc with Bernoulli potential outcomes; this is a legal subclass certificate, not a restriction of the main class. The results do not cover releases retaining raw coordinates, angle, or within-bin radius, and they do not claim transfer to curved-boundary or unknown-weight aliases for which the polynomial \(\phi\) may fail to be orthogonal to the latent first-bin weight.
honest_scope: The standing partial-identification result is the release-fiber bound \(2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta\); exact release-law-specific endpoints and the sharp maximal-diameter constant remain open through the sharp release-fiber endpoint question. The supporting statistical results give matching minimax risk and honest expected-length orders uniformly over \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), not sharp leading constants. When \(\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\), the frontier is sampling-limited at \(n^{-1/4}\); when \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the population ambiguity fixes the order-\(\Delta\) floor. Applicability requires that the observation field be exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\).
